h1: Running a happy hour that does not wreck brewpub margins
title: Happy Hours That Protect Your Margins | Craft Beer School
desc: How to run a brewpub happy hour that fills quiet hours without wrecking margins: the break-even maths, which beers to include and responsible service.
teaser: A 30 percent discount needs far more than 30 percent extra sales to pay for itself. Most happy hours are never checked.
standfirst: A happy hour can turn a dead 5 PM into a busy one. It can also teach your regulars to stop paying full price. Here is how to design one that earns its place.
sections: What a happy hour is for

A happy hour exists to fill hours that would otherwise be quiet, usually early evenings on weekdays. The aim is to bring in guests who would not have come, or to bring them earlier so they stay for dinner. If it only gives a discount to people who would have come anyway at full price, it costs money.

Before you design one, look at your POS data. Which hours are genuinely empty? Which hours are already busy? A happy hour on a slot that is already half full mostly discounts existing trade.

A discount reduces margin per drink, so you need more drinks to make the same gross profit. Here is a worked example with made-up numbers. Say a pint sells for ₹400 and costs you ₹100 in beer and excise. Your gross profit is ₹300 per pint. With 30 percent off, the price is ₹280 and gross profit is ₹180. To match the original gross profit, you need to sell 300 divided by 180, or about 1.67 times as many pints. That is 67 percent more volume for a 30 percent discount.

Run the numbers with your own costs. Our guide to beer pricing strategy shows how to calculate cost per pint.

• Limit the hours. Keep it to the genuinely quiet slot, for example 5 to 7 PM on weekdays.
  • Choose the beers. Include your high-volume core beers with lower cost, not special releases.
  • Use a fixed price rather than a percentage. Easier to understand and control.
  • Pair it with food. A food offer often drives more profitable spend than a beer discount.
  • Avoid buy-one-get-one. It encourages faster drinking and doubles the discount on the second drink.

Check your state's excise rules. Some states restrict happy hours, discounts or promotions on alcohol. Liquor advertising is limited nationally. Confirm what is allowed before you print a menu or post online.
Watch the waste and the bar

Busy happy hours put pressure on the bar. Fast pours mean more foam, more spillage and more over-pours. A busy hour at a lower price with higher waste can erase the gain. Our guide to reducing beer loss at the bar covers how to measure pour accuracy and line losses. Staff the bar properly for the rush and keep an eye on the dispense system.

A happy hour works best when guests stay after it ends. Plan for the transition: a kitchen ready to serve dinner at 7, a reason to stay such as a quiz or live music and staff who suggest the next order at full price. Track how many happy hour guests are still ordering after it ends. Our taproom economics guide shows how the evening's revenue adds up.

A discount is the bluntest way to fill quiet hours. Others often work better. A weekday quiz, a brewer's tasting, a new release launched at 6 PM, a food pairing evening or a community group that meets regularly can all bring people in at full price. Our guide to taproom events covers formats worth trying. Many brewpubs find that a reason to come beats a cheaper pint.

These ideas also build the regular crowd that keeps a taproom busy in the quiet months, which a discount rarely does. A guest who came for a quiz and met the brewer has a reason to return. A guest who came for a cheap pint will go wherever the next cheap pint is.

Discounted drinks should never mean encouraging heavy drinking. Avoid offers that reward speed or quantity. Train staff to refuse service to guests who have had too much and to offer water and alcohol-free options. Always include a good alcohol-free choice in any offer. Make it easy for guests to get home safely.

Run a happy hour for a fixed trial period, perhaps six weeks, then compare sales, gross profit and guest numbers with the same hours before. Look at total gross profit for the whole evening, not just the happy hour slot. If gross profit did not rise, change the design or stop it. A happy hour should be a tool you can switch off, not a habit your regulars depend on.
faqs: How much extra volume does a happy hour need?
It depends on your margin. In one worked example, a 30 percent discount needed about 67 percent more pints to earn the same gross profit.
Are happy hours legal in India?
It depends on the state. Some states restrict discounts or promotions on alcohol. Check your state's current excise rules.
Which beers should be in a happy hour?
Core, high-volume beers with lower cost per pint, rather than special or expensive releases.
